title: The funeral prayer (janazah)
intro: Death, the janazah prayer and how we comfort a family.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Every soul will taste death… <small>(Qur’an, Ali ‘Imran 3:185)</small>

Allah decreed that a person lives in the dunya for a set time, after which the soul returns to Allah and the body to the earth from which it was made. Death is moving from the dunya to the eternal world – the akhirah.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: One day Jibril came to the Prophet (SAW) and said: “O Muhammad! Live as you wish, but you will die in the end. Love whom you wish, but you will leave them in the end. Do what you wish – you will be rewarded (or punished) for it.” (Tabarani)

items: We must not wish for death because of a hardship: “Let none of you wish for death because of a hardship that befalls him…” <small>(Bukhari and Muslim)</small>
Whoever feels death is near should write a will (wasiyyah).
Recite the Shahadah, and often say laa ilaaha illallaah.
When a Muslim passes away, the family should repay any debts as soon as possible.

learn.html: The janazah is a special prayer for Muslims who have died. It is fard kifayah – a duty of the community that some of its members must do; if nobody does it, everyone is sinful.

items: Conditions: the person who died was a Muslim; the body has been washed (ghusl) and wrapped in a shroud (kafan); it is placed in front of the jama‘ah; its right side faces the Qiblah
Fard: standing in rows (at least three rows is good); saying four takbirs behind the imam, raising the hands only at the first

Sunnah: after the 1st takbir, Subhanaka with wa jalla thanaa’uk; after the 2nd, the salawat; after the 3rd, the janazah dua; after the 4th, the salam to the right (lowering the right hand) and to the left (lowering the left hand)

learn.html: Carrying the deceased to the graveyard and burying them is also fard kifayah for Muslims; it is sunnah to hurry in carrying the janazah. It is makruh for women to follow and see off the janazah.

items: We comfort the family with words that give patience and help them accept Allah’s decree: Innaa lillaahi wa innaa ilayhi raaji‘oon – “We belong to Allah and to Him we return.”
The grieving family answers: Innallaaha ma‘as-saabireen – “Truly, Allah is with the patient.”
Condolence has no time limit, but it is best in the first three days.
It is sunnah for relatives and neighbours to make food for the grieving family. The Prophet (SAW) said: “Prepare food for the family of Ja‘far, for what has happened has kept them busy.” (Tirmidhi)
In Bosnia there is also a traditional way of giving condolence in Turkish: Başın sağ olsun (may your head be well), answered with Dostum sağ olsun (may my friend be well too).

practice.title: Talk with your muallim
prompts: 💬 What is death? What is the janazah prayer, and what are its conditions, fard and sunnah?
🤔 Which traditional customs at a funeral are not part of Islam? Remember: what we learned as fard and wajib is the religion – everything else is tradition.
